solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Delicate shot dealing with service when returning (8)

indicatorNotes.when returning: coming back means read the pieces right to left

blocks.note: a go = a shot, an attempt

annotation.surface: A tennis player plays a soft drop shot off a returned serve.
annotation.walkthrough: The tennis words shot, service and returning all do other jobs: service is the church kind, and only the last two pieces turn round.
annotation.definitionFit: Gossamer, as an adjective, describes anything as fine and delicate as a spider's thread.

entries.clue: If heard, a dog can be found (5)

indicatorNotes.If heard: tells you to go by the sound of the words

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

annotation.surface: A remark that a dog will turn up if you listen for it.
annotation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'a cur' runs together as the verb OCCUR.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that occurs somewhere can be found there, as in 'the plant occurs in bogs'.

entries.clue: Mute used by violinist, otherwise racket pierces terribly (7)

indicatorNotes.pierces: the first pieces go through the middle of the last one

blocks.note: so = terribly, as in 'so sorry'; split S…O around the rest

annotation.surface: A complaint that a violinist's racket is painful even with the mute on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' looks like it describes the noise, but it is an intensifier. A sordino is the Italian name for the clip-on mute.
annotation.definitionFit: Sordino is the musical term for a mute placed on the bridge of a violin.

entries.clue: Soaking allotment opened by official staff (10)

indicatorNotes.opened by: the second piece comes first, opening the word

blocks.note: a mace is the ceremonial staff carried before an official
a ration is an allotted share

annotation.surface: A council allotment gets flooded when the staff open it up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Allotment' suggests a vegetable plot and 'staff' employees, but they are a RATION and the MACE carried by a mayor.
annotation.definitionFit: Maceration is softening something by soaking it in liquid.

entries.clue: Toss / sticks at the seaside (4)

blocks.note: a verb: to toss about, as a boat in waves
a hard candy sold in sticks at British holiday resorts

annotation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a stick of hard, brightly coloured candy sold at British holiday resorts, often with the town's name running through it.
annotation.definitionFit: A ship tossed on the sea rocks, and rock itself comes in sticks at the seaside.

entries.clue: Show contempt for playwright copying Psmith? (5)

blocks.note: Psmith is SMITH with a silent P put in front

annotation.surface: A question whether a playwright borrowing Wodehouse's affectation deserves scorn.
annotation.walkthrough: Psmith, a P. G. Wodehouse character, added a silent P to his plain name Smith; do the same to SHAW.
annotation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an exclamation of contempt, and as a verb means to express that contempt.

entries.clue: Innkeeper’s yearly drink cut by doctor (7)

indicatorNotes.cut by: the doctor cuts into the other letters, sitting inside them

blocks.note: one = a drink, as in 'one for the road'

annotation.surface: A landlord's annual tipple is rationed on doctor's orders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drink' as a noun, as in 'fancy one?' or 'one for the road'. Padrone is Italian for a landlord or master.
annotation.definitionFit: A padrone is the owner of an Italian inn or hotel.

entries.clue: Note struggle behind house, result of shooting there? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.behind: the struggle comes after the rest

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

annotation.surface: A fight behind a house leaves the aftermath of a shooting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' reads as gunfire at a crime scene; it is filming, and 'there' points back to the house.
annotation.definitionFit: Shooting here is filming, and a film made in your own house by amateurs is the result; 'there' ties the definition back to the house.

entries.clue: Unfriendly judge goes after successful outcome (6)

indicatorNotes.goes after: the judge's word follows the other piece

blocks.note: to try a case is to judge it

annotation.surface: A judge turns hostile after losing the verdict he wanted.
annotation.walkthrough: The judge is a verb here: courts TRY cases.
annotation.definitionFit: A wintry smile or manner is cold and unfriendly.

entries.clue: Undesirable growth of plant factory justified in report (6)

indicatorNotes.in report: a report is something spoken, so go by sound

blocks.note: a mill is a plant or factory; due = justified, deserved

annotation.surface: A report describes a factory's plant growth as unwelcome but deserved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' tempts toward greenery, but 'plant factory' is a single industrial MILL.
annotation.definitionFit: Mildew is a fungus that grows where you do not want it.

entries.clue: Former South American king provided for driver (2-3)

blocks.note: the Incas were the pre-Columbian people of Peru

annotation.surface: An Inca king is supplied with a chauffeur.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective phrase: in-car entertainment is provided for the driver.
annotation.definitionFit: In-car things, like a satnav, are for the driver's use.

entries.clue: Bad spirit more or less reflected a lack of claret (9)

indicatorNotes.reflected: a mirror image, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: no Médoc: Médoc is a claret, a red Bordeaux

annotation.surface: Someone is in a foul mood, roughly speaking, because the claret has run out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bad spirit' looks like a grumpy mood or a poor wine; it is a demon. Médoc is a Bordeaux region whose red wine is claret.
annotation.definitionFit: A cacodemon is an evil spirit, from Greek kakos, bad.

entries.clue: Mistake during dive, leaving five engineers behind (8)

indicatorNotes.during: the mistake happens in the middle of the dive
indicatorNotes.leaving: the five goes out of the word

blocks.note: DIVE without V, the Roman five; split D…IE
to err is to make a mistake

annotation.surface: A diver fumbles, and five engineers are left behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Behind' reads as left in the rear; it is the definition, a noun for the backside.
annotation.definitionFit: Derriere, from French, is a polite word for the behind.

entries.clue: Daughter first mentioned unopened window (6)

indicatorNotes.unopened: the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: FORMER (first mentioned) without its first letter

annotation.surface: A girl was the first to mention the window left shut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The former' is the first of two things mentioned; take its F away.
annotation.definitionFit: A dormer is a window set upright in a sloping roof.

entries.clue: Ring sailor in race that’s lost time — he’ll protest (10)

indicatorNotes.that’s lost: the sailor's word drops the time letter

blocks.note: to ring = to bell, give someone a ring

blocks.clueFragment: sailor in race that’s lost time
blocks.note: YACHTER (a sailor in a race) without T, time

annotation.surface: A sailor beaten in a race phones in a complaint.
annotation.walkthrough: The sailor is not the usual AB or TAR: the phrase 'sailor in race' gives the whole word YACHTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A bellyacher is a chronic complainer, one who will always protest.

entries.clue: Frankly weird present heralded by hearts on card (7,7)

indicatorNotes.heralded by: the hearts-and-card piece comes before the rest
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, hearts go after the card

blocks.note: a card is a joker, a wit
to serve = to present, as a dish

annotation.surface: A card-game player frankly finds a hand led with hearts a strange gift.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Card' and 'hearts' belong to a pack of cards, but card here is a witty person, a WIT.
annotation.definitionFit: Reserve is restraint in speech, so talking with none held back is talking frankly; an adverb phrase for an adverb.

entries.clue: Thin cleaner not thin enough to fit around piano (9)

indicatorNotes.to fit around: the phrase goes round the piano

annotation.surface: A slim cleaning tool is still too fat to get round the piano.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thin' appears twice to pull opposite ways: a thin tool, and a phrase meaning its opposite, TOO THICK.
annotation.definitionFit: A toothpick is a thin stick for cleaning between the teeth.

entries.clue: Silly wet males not for Germaine Greer, say (5,2,7)

indicatorNotes.Silly: a silly arrangement is a mixed-up one

annotation.surface: A jibe that the feminist Germaine Greer has no time for feeble men.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits Greer's feminism perfectly, which hides that she is the definition as an example of a writer.
annotation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer, author of The Female Eunuch, is a noted woman of letters.

entries.clue: Prisoner with muscles died gripping that bunk (7)

indicatorNotes.gripping: the muscles and died hold the prisoner inside

annotation.surface: A muscular convict dies clinging to his prison bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a prison bed; it is the verb, as in 'do a bunk', meaning run off.
annotation.definitionFit: To bunk or do a bunk is British slang for running away, the same as abscond.

entries.clue: Number one hit, of course? (3,4)

blocks.note: reads as a chart-topping record; meant as the first stroke played
reads as 'naturally'; meant as on a golf course

annotation.surface: A chart-topping song that was bound to succeed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number one hit' reads as a chart-topper and 'of course' as naturally; both are golf, the first shot struck on a course.
annotation.definitionFit: The tee shot is a golfer's first hit on each hole.

entries.clue: Hasty dairy supplier not quite filling tin (6)

indicatorNotes.not quite: something not quite complete stops just short, so the word loses its final letter
indicatorNotes.filling: a filling sits inside something, so the shortened udder goes inside the tin

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin; split S…N
UDDER, the cow's milk supply, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone rushes to fill a tin from a cow.
annotation.walkthrough: The dairy supplier is not a milkman but the cow's UDDER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something done quickly and without warning or thought.

entries.clue: Real man using lasso under pressure (6)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, the man sits below the pressure

annotation.surface: A genuine cowboy stays cool with a lasso under stress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Real man' reads as a unit, but Real is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper job or a real job: both mean genuine.

entries.clue: Work over there has Hebe in the middle (6)

indicatorNotes.in the middle: the answer sits inside the words

annotation.surface: A painting or poem over there shows the goddess Hebe at its centre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun, an artwork; with 'over' it is a verb for rehashing.
annotation.definitionFit: To rehash old material is to work it over again.

entries.clue: Presume Spooner’s cook specially shaped dish? (4,4)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: the Reverend Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: bake = cook; a mould is a shaped dish, as for jelly

annotation.surface: A guess about what Spooner's cook will serve in a fancy dish.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of BAKE and MOULD.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'may I make so bold as to ask' means 'may I presume to ask', taking a liberty.

entries.clue: Prison officers were kept in by delay (5)

blocks.note: of = by, as in 'the plays of Shakespeare'

annotation.surface: Prison officers had to stay late because of a delay.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the officers the warders; they are the inmates. An Oflag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for officers.
annotation.definitionFit: Oflag, short for Offizierslager, was a German camp where captured officers were held.

entries.clue: Something for the offertory when in church? (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the word for when goes inside church

blocks.note: as = when, as in 'as I left'

annotation.surface: A question about what goes in the collection plate at church.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a churchgoer's question, and the wordplay answers it with 'when' placed in church.
annotation.definitionFit: The offertory is the collection of money during a church service.

entries.clue: Learning lover’s posh but heartless, fancy him a lot (9)

indicatorNotes.fancy: a fancy arrangement is a rearranged one

annotation.surface: A swot's girlfriend is well-bred but cold, yet fancies him madly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lover' and 'fancy' suggest romance; fancy is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: The Greek roots philo- (loving) and math- (learning) translate straight into the definition.

entries.clue: Very hearty sandwiches to cut into triangles? (5)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the hearty word holds the very letter between its parts

annotation.surface: Instructions for serving generous sandwiches in triangles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' is the verb, not the food; the question mark flags that cutting a sandwich diagonally is just one way to halve.
annotation.definitionFit: Cutting a square sandwich corner to corner halves it into two triangles.

entries.clue: Assigned to classes, letting name go on a list (5)

indicatorNotes.letting: with 'go', the name is let out of the word

blocks.clueFragment: Assigned to classes, letting name go

annotation.surface: Pupils are sorted into classes and dropped from the register.
annotation.walkthrough: 'List' reads as a register, but it is a ship's lean, and a raked stage or mast is sloped.
annotation.definitionFit: A list is a tilt, so something raked is set at a slant, on a list.

entries.clue: One man’s retreat out of Moscow, primarily the stuff of history (8)

indicatorNotes.out of: something taken out of a place is removed from it, so M comes out of the retreat
indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so only Moscow's first letter is used

blocks.note: a hermitage is a hermit's retreat

annotation.surface: Napoleon's retreat from Moscow became the stuff of history.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retreat out of Moscow' conjures Napoleon's army; the retreat is a hermit's HERMITAGE, which loses Moscow's M.
annotation.definitionFit: Heritage is what history hands down to us.
